classification.difficultyReason: 1D Q83: Structural selection, multiple connected steps, proof or admissible-case reasoning. The question itself provides the difference-of-cubes identity. Substituting a negative second term handles the sum; page 20 supplies the rationalisation procedure.

content.prompt:
Use the identity $a^3-b^3=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)$ to rationalise the denominator of
$$\frac1{1+\sqrt[3]2}.$$

answer.worked:
Let $t=\sqrt[3]2$. The supplied identity with $a=1$, $b=-t$ gives $(1+t)(1-t+t^2)=1+t^3$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac1{1+\sqrt[3]2}&=\frac{1-\sqrt[3]2+\sqrt[3]4}{(1+\sqrt[3]2)(1-\sqrt[3]2+\sqrt[3]4)}\\\frac1{1+\sqrt[3]2}&=\frac{1-\sqrt[3]2+\sqrt[3]4}{1+2}\\\frac1{1+\sqrt[3]2}&=\frac{1-\sqrt[3]2+\sqrt[3]4}{3}.\end{align*}$$
